questions.q: The pure wealth-maximisation objective preferred over profit maximisation primarily because it:
o: Considers timing, risk and magnitude of cash flows and avoids myopic accounting profit
questions.why: Wealth maximisation uses discounted cash flows (timing+risk) and market value; profit maximisation is accounting-based, ambiguous in timing and ignores risk.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — objective-function questions anchor Ch 1 every attempt Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Profit is an opinion about a year; wealth is a valuation of all years.
mem.link: Chapter 1 — Financial Policy and Corporate Strategy

questions.q: Under the Companies Act CSR provisions tested in the corporate-strategy chapter, companies meeting the prescribed thresholds must spend at least what share of average net profits (computed per the Act) in the immediately preceding three financial years?
questions.why: Section 135: average net profit per Section 198 for the immediately preceding three years × 2%, subject to threshold; unspent amounts follow the transfer/ carry-forward rules in the Act — new-scheme syllabus places CSR under Ch 1 strategy context.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — statutory thresholds embedded in strategy are crisp 1-markers AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: CSR is 2% — the number with a deadline and a ledger.

o: Net margin × asset turnover × equity multiplier
questions.why: ROE = (NI/Sales) × (Sales/TA) × (TA/Equity) — efficiency of margin, usage of assets, and leverage; the 5-factor adds tax/interest layers.

questions.q: An aggressive current-assets financing policy uses:
o: Short-term sources to finance part of permanent CA (low cost, high risk)
questions.why: Aggressive: short-term liabilities fund permanent CA too — cheaper but refinancing/renewal risk; conservative: opposite; matching: permanent to LT.
